identity.title: WAFT: Warping-Alone Field Transforms for Optical Flow

problem.claim: Design a simple, effective, and flexible method for optical flow.

gap.claim: The authors challenge the conventional assumption that cost-volume construction is necessary for strong optical-flow performance.

contributions.claim: WAFT replaces RAFT-style cost volumes with high-resolution warping in a meta-architecture with minimal inductive biases and limited reliance on custom designs.
The authors report top benchmark rankings, strong zero-shot generalization on KITTI, and faster inference than competitive existing methods.
The authors provide code and model weights.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present warping-alone field transforms as a simple alternative to cost-volume-based optical-flow architectures.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that WAFT ranks first on Spring, Sintel, and KITTI benchmarks.
The authors report the best zero-shot generalization on KITTI.
The authors report 1.3–4.1× faster speed than existing methods with competitive accuracy, including 1.3× versus Flowformer++ and 4.1× versus CCMR+.

narrative_sequence.summary: Introduces WAFT as a simple optical-flow method.
Replaces cost volumes with high-resolution warping while retaining similarity to RAFT.
Uses a flexible, minimally biased meta-architecture and questions the necessity of cost volumes.
Reports leading benchmark rankings, KITTI zero-shot performance, and speed advantages over competitive methods.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a specific architectural substitution—cost volumes replaced by high-resolution warping—to both accuracy and memory-cost claims.

lessons.interpretation: A focused mechanism-to-benefit framing can make a method’s central design hypothesis easy to evaluate.
lessons.application: State the replaced component, its substitute, and the intended resource or accuracy consequence in one contribution claim.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the method’s benefits arise from many interacting components that cannot be isolated at abstract level.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify benchmark metrics, numerical accuracy results, dataset splits, or evaluation protocols.
The speed comparisons lack hardware, implementation, and measurement conditions.
The meaning and scope of “best zero-shot generalization” on KITTI are not defined.
No ablation or evidence isolating high-resolution warping from other design choices is reported.
